hostRead.heading: Reading files on this machine
hostRead.intro: The folders the assistant may read files from on this machine. It can list them and read text files, with passwords and keys hidden, and it never writes. Nothing is readable until you save a folder here. Files that look like secrets (keys, .env files, credentials, browser profiles) stay closed even inside a folder. The node reads with the rights of its own service account: what that account may not read stays unreadable until you grant the right on the machine (see the node installation guide, section 10a).

hostRead.saved: Saved. The node picks the change up the next time it checks in.

yield.heading: Consideration for local use
yield.summaryOn: On: the node freezes its models while someone uses the keyboard or mouse (the last {{idle}} s), other programs use more than {{cpu}} % of the CPU, or the machine runs on battery. Models are unloaded after a pause of {{unload}} min.
yield.summaryOff: Off: the node keeps working while the machine is used.
yield.priorityOn: Models always run at the lowest process priority.
yield.hint: Frozen models continue at the same place; an answer in progress waits and goes on afterwards. A node without a dedicated GPU (a laptop) has this on by default, a node with one has it off. If keyboard and mouse cannot be seen (Windows service), CPU load and battery still work.
yield.enabled: Freeze the models while the machine is in use
yield.low_priority: Run llama-server and llama-bench at the lowest process priority
yield.idle_seconds: In use until this long after the last input (s)
yield.cpu_percent: Other programs' CPU load that counts as use (%, 0 = off)
yield.resume_seconds: Continue when the CPU load has been low for (s)
yield.unload_after_pause_seconds: Unload the models after a pause of (s, 0 = never)

care.heading: Care of the memory
care.intro: Once a night and when nothing else is going on, the assistant checks notes it can no longer be sure of – with read-only tools only, never on your documents or the web. It corrects what it can prove, asks when you said it yourself, strikes expired short-term states and puts notes nobody needs into the archive. Every step is a version you can undo.
